provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The task is Latin-square completion: holes (original colour 0, here palette[0]) are filled so each row and column contains each of the four colours (palette[1..4]) exactly once. The constraint is symmetric under all D4 transforms (rows<->columns, reversals preserve the row/column sets), so the emitted program works directly on the visible grid with no coordinate change; only colour roles are specialised via palette constants. It mirrors the generator's mechanism (repeatedly fill any row/column with a single hole by its missing colour), adds single-candidate cell deduction as in the archived solver, and falls back to backtracking. Under the generator, every hole was carved from a then-complete line, so the deduction always completes uniquely.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the hole colour is palette[0] and fill colours are palette[1..4] (true for all generated 4x4 scenes). For non-4x4 grids it infers the colour set from the query and demonstration outputs, which is outside the constructor's domain. If a puzzle were unsolvable the partially deduced grid is returned.
